Fixture: 62_mixed_24x24_lossless.jxl
24x24 RGB, gradient | 1-pixel checkerboard, mathematically lossless, effort 7
-- OPEN BUG REPRODUCER, and the one that localises it

Purpose
-------
The smallest LOSSLESS stream in the open H.5 weighted-predictor family, and
the first that fails on a channel whose MA leaves are `Gradient` rather than
`SelfCorrecting`. It is the same source shape as VarDCT fixtures 54/57 --
half smooth gradient, half 1-pixel magenta/cyan checkerboard -- shrunk until
minimal:

  * 23x23 decodes bit-exactly; 24x24 fails. 20/21/22 also decode.
  * Every content simplification tested at 24x24 decodes bit-exactly:
    checkerboard only, gradient only, flat right half, black/white
    checkerboard, and greyscale. Both halves and the 1-pixel period are
    required.

cjxl palettes all three colour channels, so the coded image is three 1-row
palette meta-channels (36, 24 and 12 entries) followed by three 24x24 index
channels, with an 11-leaf MA tree over 5 entropy clusters that branches on
property 15 (`max_error`) at five nodes.

What it establishes
-------------------
All three palettes and the entire first index channel (576 samples) decode
bit-exactly. The second index channel diverges at (11, 5) -- the last column
of the gradient half, i.e. the sample whose `NE` neighbour is the first
checkerboard sample. There:

  W3 40  N3 32  NE3 184   subpred = [192, 108, 55, 69]   our prediction 151
  required prediction is in [37, 44]  (the decoded residual is 0 and the
  correct sample is 5, so `(prediction + 3) >> 3` must be 5)

and 233 forced-context checkpoints pass before it, so the entropy stream is
still synchronised. The required prediction is **unreachable**: any weighted
average of the sub-predictions lies in [55, 192], and the clamp can only
additionally yield `min(W3,N3,NE3) = 32` or `max(W3,N3,NE3) = 184`. That
rules out the weights, `err_sum`, the clamp gating, the clamp bounds and the
`max_error` selection all at once, and points at the sub-predictor formulas
themselves (or the `true_err` values feeding them). See
docs/experiments/2026-08-03-h52-subpredictor-localisation.md.

                tools/make-debug-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was used,
                converted, or consulted. 24x24 8-bit RGB (PPM P6):
                  x <  12: R = x * 255 / 11, G = y * 255 / 23,
                           B = (x + y) mod 256          smooth gradient
                  x >= 12: magenta (255,0,255) / cyan (0,255,255),
                           alternating every pixel by (x + y) parity

                sha256 1c854b52969d541eb13ee56350fdac21271dd3632a6d52e1e3318a7024ff1504

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PPM byte-identical to the source (checked on every run of
tools/make-debug-fixtures.sh), so the stream is conformant and the divergence
is JPXL's.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
